podcast.title: Relationship with Michael Hutchence
podcast.body: British TV host Paula Yates had a relationship with Michael Hutchence of INXS. "She had a thing with Michael Hutchins of an excess at the time of his death."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rock Star Kids ｜ From the Archives

xref.title: First Meeting with Paula Yates (1985)
xref.body: As a guest on the British TV show *The Tube* in 1985, he met host Paula Yates, then partnered with Bob Geldof. He immediately asked her to return to his hotel room; she declined, but a strong connection was established, potentially initiating an affair. "In 1985, Hutchins was a guest on the British TV show The Tube. The host was Paula Yates, and she, for the last 10 years, had been with Bob Geldoff, he of the Bumpton Rats and the organizer of Live Aid."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Big Breakfast Interview (1994)
xref.body: In 1994, he reunited with Paula Yates on her show *The Big Breakfast* for a seven-minute interview conducted on a bed, with both entwined. The media widely labeled it "the most sexually charged TV interview of all time," and it was watched by two million people. During the interview, he discussed a greatest hits album, ending a contract with an American record company, and scaling back his clubbing habits. "In 1994, they met again for Paula's new show The Big Breakfast. As soon as it was over, the media was calling that interview the most sexually charged TV interview of all time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Relationship with Paula Yates and Tabloid Coverage (1995-1997)
xref.body: Hutchence was involved in a complex and unhealthy breakup with British TV personality Paula Yates, the mother of his children, by 1995. Their relationship was characterized by extensive drug and alcohol use and became a prominent subject of tabloid coverage. "By 1995, he was locked into a complex breakup with Paula Yates, the British TV person."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Split from Helena Christensen (March 1995)
xref.body: He separated from Helena Christensen in March 1995 after being discovered with Paula Yates in a hotel, a development that became a major tabloid sensation in England. "Hutchinson, Christianson, split up after he was caught with Yates in a hotel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chelsea Drug Raid (September 1996)
xref.body: In September 1996, he was implicated in a drug raid at Paula Yates's Chelsea home, where opium and smoking pipes were found. Both he and Yates claimed the drugs had been planted by employees. "Michael and Paula responded by saying that the drugs were planted."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Paranoia and Mental State (1997)
xref.body: In early 1997, amidst wedding plans with Paula Yates, he became increasingly paranoid, believing his phones and homes were bugged. During promo and final tours that year, he appeared tired, older than his 37 years, and exhibited erratic behavior during shows. "He had become paranoid, claiming that his phones and houses were bugged."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cremation and Ash Dispute
xref.body: Following his cremation, a significant dispute arose over his ashes involving his family, Paula Yates, and the band. "And later when Michael was cremated, there was a big fight over his ashes between his family, Paula, and the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fatherhood and Custody Strain
xref.body: He became a father to Heavenly Hiraani Tiger Lily with Paula Yates. Despite his pride in fatherhood, he was caught in the midst of the contentious custody battle between Yates and Bob Geldof, a strain that worsened his addictions and existing predilections. "Michael and Paula were the parents of a baby girl named Heveli, Herani, Tiger Lily. And while he was proud to be a father, Michael was caught in the middle of everything between Paula and Bob."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Call with Bob Geldof
xref.body: Between 4 AM and 5 AM on the day of his death, he made two calls to Bob Geldof, engaging in a loud, 20-minute argument. He attempted to persuade Geldof to lift an injunction against Paula Yates, allowing the children to come to Australia for Christmas, but Geldof refused. Hutchence was heard screaming phrases like, "your children hate you. I'm their father, little man." "Hutchins called Bob Geldoff twice. Michael wanted to persuade Bob to drop the cordon junction against Paula and let the three kids come to Australia for Christmas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Phone Call with Paula Yates (5:38 AM, November 22)
xref.body: At 5:38 AM on November 22, Paula Yates called him and later described him as sounding "really desperate." "At 5.38 a.m., Paula called. Three later said that Michael sounded really desperate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mailing Last Letters
xref.body: Early on the morning of his death, looking "really rough," he visited the hotel front desk to ask a clerk to mail two letters: one addressed to Paula Yates and another to a friend in Hong Kong. This was the last time anyone saw him alive. "Early in the morning and looking really rough, he went on to the front desk and asked the clerk to mail two letters that he had written. One to Paula and the other to a friend in Hong Kong."

xref.title: Official Cause of Death and Alternative Theories
xref.body: His death on November 22, 1997, was officially ruled a suicide. However, in 1999, Paula Yates suggested on *60 Minutes* Australia that he died from auto-erotic asphyxiation gone wrong, a theory the coroner explicitly rejected due to lack of forensic evidence. This theory gained widespread belief, fueled by Hutchence's known sexual kinks, his mother's mention of him being with sadomasochists, and his own comments about seeking the "ultimate sexual high." "Again, the corner rule that Michael Hutchins died by his own hand in that hotel room on November 22, 1997. But then in 1999, Paula Yates made a suggestion. Totally contrary to everything she'd said up until that point. On the Australian version of 60 minutes, she intimated that Michael may have died as the result of solo sex play gone wrong. Auto-erotic asphyxiation, which he took too far."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Wedding Plans with Paula Yates
xref.body: He and Paula Yates were planning to marry in Tahiti as soon as they could find the time. "They were going to get married in Tahiti just as soon as the two of them could find the time."
